item.title: EU INC | 2026-W11
item.description:
eu-inc Weekly | 2026-W11

A week of institutional weight and new friction: Bruegel extended the 28th regime concept beyond startup incorporation into capital markets, while a new compliance counter-argument emerged challenging whether EU-INC actually reduces the regulatory burden companies face in practice.

This Week

What is the 28th legal regime? Where have I seen it before? (European Law Blog) -- Scholarly analysis situating the 28th regime within the history of EU harmonization attempts, offering the clearest academic framing of how this initiative compares to past single-market projects.

The 28th Regime - A strategic necessity for scaling European Innovation (EBN) -- Position paper from the European Business and Innovation Centres network, which supports 30,000+ startups and SMEs annually, making it the broadest practitioner-network endorsement of the regime yet published.

New Arguments

  • ✅ Extending the 28th regime via a building-block approach to capital markets -- not just startup incorporation -- would unlock deeper EU financial integration (Rebecca Christie, Bruegel: 28th regimes to help Europe's capital markets)
  • ❌ EU-INC simplifies incorporation but leaves companies exposed to thousands of pages of evolving legal requirements across 27 jurisdictions, including the EU AI Act, so the compliance burden is not actually solved (@firstaimovers)

Radar

  • 🧑 Robin Wauters identified as an EU-Inc ecosystem builder in a YouTube interview -- first practitioner voice from the EU-Inc advocacy side to appear in the knowledge base
  • 📡 The Economist published a bullish piece on European tech without mentioning EU-INC, signaling the concept has not yet broken through to top-tier general business press (@SebJohnsonUK)

item.title: EU INC | 2026-W10
item.description:
eu-inc Weekly | 2026-W10

A quiet week on the EU Inc front -- no major legislative moves, but the analytical layer thickened as law firms and business press caught up to the January Davos moment.

This Week

EU Inc. -- The Truly European Company Structure (McDermott Will & Emery) -- A major international law firm publishes its first detailed client briefing on EU Inc., framing von der Leyen's January 20 Davos announcement as a historic turning point.

EU Inc. May Solve Legal Issues, But Scaling Across Borders Still Depends on How Teams Work (European Business Review) -- Argues that legal harmonization is necessary but not sufficient, as operational and HR complexity across member states persists regardless of corporate structure.

Startups fordern Verordnung zur EU Inc (Börsen-Zeitung) -- German startup community pushes specifically for a regulation (directly applicable) rather than a directive, and flags capital gains tax triggers when founders relocate between EU countries.

What is EU-INC and its plan to make European businesses borderless? (Euronews) -- Clean explainer piece useful for briefing newcomers to the topic.

New Arguments

  • ❌ A unified corporate form does not remove the underlying operational fragmentation -- tax, employment law, and team management remain jurisdiction-specific (European Business Review)
  • ❌ Several EU member states impose capital gains tax when a founder relocates their company to another EU country, a friction EU Inc. would not automatically resolve (Börsen-Zeitung)

Radar

  • 🧑 McDermott Will & Emery and Orrick both publish substantive EU Inc. briefings this cycle -- signals the major transatlantic law firm tier is now actively advising clients on the proposal.
